key_insight: Coupling mobile dissolved Cu with immobile precipitates reveals that Cu depletion and precipitate-induced transport barriers can accelerate electromigration failure and invalidate simple Arrhenius lifetime extrapolation.
engineering_relevance: Al–Cu interconnect reliability predictions should account for Cu solubility, precipitate blocking, microstructure and end conditions rather than treating all Cu as mobile.
method: Couple an evolving Cu field to the one-dimensional Korhonen stress equation.
Simulate random grain maps for wide (10 μm), narrow (3 μm) and near-bamboo lines.
Track nucleation times and sites, immortal fractions and Black’s-law parameters.
evidence_signal: Using 1,000 grain maps per condition at 200 °C, the model predicts 1.15–1.20-fold shorter median nucleation times with Cu depletion than with immobile Cu; separate temperature analysis finds high-temperature fits can overestimate lifetime at 150 °C by up to 2.33-fold.
watch_item: Agreement is qualitative: the model does not reproduce cathode-side Cu peaks or the longer lifetimes observed in narrow lines.
paper_title: Solute-Aware Stochastic Korhonen Model of Electromigration in Wide vs Near-Bamboo Al-Cu Lines
